newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq hopes halting fire will defuse crisis.
newsitem.headline: Iraq hopes halting fire will defuse crisis.

text.p: Iraq said on Saturday it hoped its decision to halt missile attacks on U.S. and allied warplanes enforcing no-fly zones would help defuse the military standoff with Washington.

"Iraq, by suspending its military reaction to violations of our national airspace, until further notice, provides another proof of its strong keenness to avoid the eruption of crises," the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya said in a front-page editorial.
"It also shows its clear adherence to the solving of problems via peaceful means within the framework of respect for national sovereignty, international law and the U.N. charter."
The U.S. decision to dispatch warships, aircarft carriers and bombers close to Iraq illustrated that Washington was applying "a cowboy method" in dealing with events, it said.
"Iraq, keen to pull the rug from under the feet of American administration...decided to suspend reaction to the violations of its airspace by U.S. and other planes," Jumhouriya said.

In a surprise move, Iraq backed down on Friday on a pledge to shoot at Western planes patrolling its airspace. The move came just hours after U.S. Stealth bombers arrived in Kuwait as part of a U.S. military buildup in the Gulf which also includes the dispatch of 5,000 more troops.
